key_insight: A 4000+ qubit quantum annealer was used to realize a two-dimensional false-vacuum system where domain growth becomes resonantly accelerated and nearly ballistic rather than being limited by slow nucleation.
engineering_relevance: This demonstrates that large-scale quantum hardware can probe nonequilibrium metastable dynamics in a controllable way, with potential relevance to quantum simulation, materials dynamics, and field-theory analogs.
method: Programmed a 2D quantum Ising model on a quantum annealer with a metastable spin-polarized false vacuum.
Seeded a bubble and tuned the longitudinal field to trigger resonant single-spin flips at the domain boundary.
Compared experiment with tensor-network simulations and stochastic circuit models to characterize growth and interface broadening.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports experimental observation of nearly ballistic true-vacuum domain growth with sub-ballistic interface broadening, supported by matching tensor-network and stochastic-model results.
watch_item: The resonant regime appears to depend on a finely tuned field value and boundary kinetics, so robustness beyond the specific annealer setting may be limited.
paper_title: Resonant false vacuum decay in two dimensions on a 4000-qubit quantum annealer
